title: Higher prices for customers who do not switch
summary: In energy, insurance and banking, existing customers who do not shop around often pay more than new ones. The ACCC found standing electricity offers acted as a 'loyalty tax' on inert consumers (2018), and the Productivity Commission found the major banks offered inferior products to customers unlikely to change providers.
direction_rationale: When few customers switch, firms can charge their existing customers more, which weakens the pressure to compete on price.

industries.name: On Selling Electricity and Electricity Market Operation

assessment.summary: Firms charge loyal customers more than new ones in several essential services. Weak switching dulls price competition; the default electricity offers in the register were a response.
